key_insight: AgentODE uses an LLM to propose ODE models and then refines parameter distributions from summary statistics to discover interpretable dynamics when patient-level data are scarce.
clinical_relevance: This could support privacy-preserving mechanistic modeling for rare diseases, helping researchers infer disease processes from small cohorts without needing individual-level data.
method: A tool-augmented inference agent updates parameter distributions in a diagnosis–update loop
Uses population-level summary statistics rather than raw patient trajectories
evidence_signal: The authors tested AgentODE on three benchmark problems and two clinical datasets, including RDEB with only 231 observations from 46 patients.
watch_item: Results depend on summary-statistic quality and LLM-guided structure proposals, so incorrect summaries or model bias could still yield plausible but wrong mechanisms.
paper_title: LLM-Guided ODE Discovery and Parameter Inference from Small-Cohort Aggregate Data
